question: Is a per-root identity partition for shadow content worth the architecture work it would take?
ceiling: The opt arm is the cheapest thing that could capture the whole win: it hands shadow content a per-root identity token and nothing else, and it does not read the root's own sheets. A sound partition needs that per-root scan on top, so the sound build can only be SLOWER than what F4 measures. A ceiling that does not clear the floor therefore settles the question; a ceiling that clears it authorises designing the sound partition and nothing more.

arms.base: same bundle, __styleShareShadowRootTwins:false — released behaviour, shadow content reads in full

promotionExcludedReason: A sound partition has to keep :host() and ::slotted() splitting intact while partitioning shadow CONTENT. The ceiling arm does not model that at all, so these two scenes are measured (and a regression in either rejects the partition) but cannot carry the promotion case.
parityReason: Every fixture must be byte-identical across the two arms. On this fixture set the ceiling arm is expected to agree everywhere, so an empty exemption list is the strongest available contract; a future fixture that makes the ceiling arm legitimately unsound goes here with a written reason rather than silently widening the gate.

thresholdMeaning.practicalFloorPct: A PREREGISTERED PRACTICAL FLOOR for whether architecture work is worth doing, NOT a significance threshold. 1% is the smallest wall effect that would pay for a per-root sheet scan, a per-root property universe, per-root pseudo gates, per-root selector vectors, slot handling and their own invalidation story. It carries no claim that 1% is detectable here; whether this instrument can resolve 1% is exactly what INCONCLUSIVE reports.
thresholdMeaning.materialRegressionPct: A ceiling that is SLOWER than released by more than this rejects the partition on its own, regardless of any other fixture.
thresholdMeaning.signConvention: The harness reports (slot2/slot1 - 1) * 100, so a NEGATIVE percentage means the ceiling arm was FASTER. Every threshold above is therefore read as an IMPROVEMENT MAGNITUDE: promotion needs an aggregate lower bound above practicalFloorPct in improvement terms, rejection needs every splitting-free fixture's aggregate upper bound below it, and a material regression is a negative improvement beyond materialRegressionPct. Getting this backwards turns every win into a regression, so lib/decide.mjs exposes improvementOf() and the contracts pin the sign.

instrument.outerNullEnvelopeSource: R9 hosted self-null calibration, run 37097245291: maximum absolute self-null 95% CI bound over the whole preregistered matrix
instrument.outerNullEnvelopeMeaning: An OUTER envelope on NULL quantities only, adopted from the completed calibration as the widest null excursion the hosted rig is known to produce. It says nothing about the effect arm: 5% cannot establish, refute or bound a 1% effect, and no fixture verdict is ever derived from it.
instrument.grossMaxPairLogSdMeaning: Kept SEPARATE from the envelope and deliberately coarse: a per-runner paired-log-ratio SD above this is a gross instability signal that voids the runner's sample regardless of what its confidence interval says. This is the same value the R9 calibration preregistered.
instrument.perRunnerDecision: forbidden — no single VM may answer the 1% question

settle.why: playwright install --with-deps spikes CPU and disk, and the ambient gate samples immediately. This waits for the runner to go quiet before the gate does, and is adaptive: it returns as soon as three consecutive samples are under the ceiling.

statistics.unit: one log-point per fresh hosted runner
statistics.ci: Student-t 95% over the runner-level log points, identical semantics to the calibrated R9 self-null
statistics.pooling: forbidden — per-call and per-block observations are never pooled across VMs
statistics.heterogeneity: reported per fixture as Q, df, I², tau² and tau(log), plus the median within-run block SD
statistics.replicates: never added automatically; INCONCLUSIVE records that the present instrument cannot settle 1%

decision.REJECT_PARTITION: Every splitting-free shadow fixture has an aggregate 95% CI UPPER bound below practicalFloorPct, OR any aggregate shadow fixture shows a material regression beyond materialRegressionPct, with instrument controls valid.
decision.PROMISING: At least one splitting-free shadow fixture has an aggregate 95% CI LOWER bound above practicalFloorPct, controls valid, and no material regression. CONTINUE_TO_ENGINES.
decision.INCONCLUSIVE: Neither of the above. The ceiling sits near the floor and this instrument cannot separate it. Do NOT add replicates automatically.
decision.INCOMPLETE_EVIDENCE: A blocked settle or ambient gate, a missing matrix cell, an inadmissible cell, or a missing report. Zero evidence can never read as a win.
decision.PROVENANCE_FAILURE: Policy, bundle, measurement-hash, fixture-identity or runner-identity drift. Never a performance statement.

staging.chromium: Primary stage, 8 fresh runners. Produces REJECT_PARTITION, PROMISING or INCONCLUSIVE.
staging.engines: Cross-engine guard, Firefox and WebKit 4 fresh runners each. Runs ONLY when chromium returned PROMISING, to save public runner minutes. Aggregated independently per engine and never averaged with chromium or with each other.

engineGuard.requirement: Per engine, independently: controls valid, no material regression, and direction consistent with the chromium finding.

purpose: Falsifier. It can reject the per-root partition, or authorise DESIGNING it. It can never promote it to production.
